name: ping
description: Send ICMP ECHO_REQUEST to network hosts

options.name: -A
options.description: Audible. Output a bell (ASCII 0x07) character when no packet is received before the next packet is transmitted.

options.name: -a
options.description: Audible. Include a bell (ASCII 0x07) character in the output when any packet is received. This option is ignored if other format options are present

options.name: -b
options.description: Bind the socket to interface boundif for sending. This option is an Apple addition

options.name: -C
options.description: Prohibit the socket from using the cellular network interface. This option is an Apple addition

options.name: -c
options.description: Stop after sending (and receiving) count ECHO_RESPONSE packets. If this option is not specified, ping will operate until inter- rupted.

options.name: -D
options.description: Set the Don't Fragment bit

options.name: -d
options.description: Set the SO_DEBUG option on the socket being used

options.name: -f
options.description: Flood ping. Outputs packets as fast as they come back or one hundred times per second, whichever is more.

options.name: -G
options.description: Sweepmaxsize Specify the maximum size of ICMP payload when sending sweeping pings. This option is required for ping sweeps

options.name: -g
options.description: Specify the size of ICMP payload to start with when sending sweeping pings

options.name: -h
options.description: Specify the number of bytes to increment the size of ICMP payload after each sweep when sending sweeping pings

options.name: -I
options.description: Source multicast packets with the given interface address. This flag only applies if the ping destination is a multicast address

options.name: -i
options.description: Wait wait seconds between sending each packet. The default is to wait for one second between each packet.

options.name: -k
options.description: Specifies the traffic class to use for sending ICMP packets. By default ping uses the control traffic class (CTL). This option is an Apple addition

options.name: -K
options.description: Specifies the network service type to use for sending ICMP pack- ets.

options.name: -L
options.description: Suppress loopback of multicast packets. This flag only applies if the ping destination is a multicast address

options.name: -l
options.description: If preload is specified, ping sends that many packets as fast as possible before falling into its normal mode of behavior.

options.name: -M
options.description: Use ICMP_MASKREQ or ICMP_TSTAMP instead of ICMP_ECHO. For mask, print the netmask of the remote machine.

options.name: -m
options.description: Set the IP Time To Live for outgoing packets. If not specified, the kernel uses the value of the net.inet.ip.ttl MIB variable

options.name: -n
options.description: Numeric output only. No attempt will be made to lookup symbolic names for host addresses

options.name: -o
options.description: Exit successfully after receiving one reply packet

options.name: -P
options.description: Policy specifies IPsec policy for the ping session. For details please refer to ipsec(4) and ipsec_set_policy(3)

options.name: -p
options.description: You may specify up to 16 'pad' bytes to fill out the packet you send. This is useful for diagnosing data-dependent problems in a network.

options.name: -Q
options.description: Somewhat quiet output. Don't display ICMP error messages that are in response to our query messages.

options.name: -q
options.description: Quiet output. Nothing is displayed except the summary lines at startup time and when finished

options.name: -R
options.description: Record route. Includes the RECORD_ROUTE option in the ECHO_REQUEST packet and displays the route buffer on returned packets.

options.name: -r
options.description: Bypass the normal routing tables and send directly to a host on an attached network. If the host is not on a directly-attached network, an error is returned.

options.name: -S
options.description: Use the following IP address as the source address in outgoing packets.

options.name: -s
options.description: Specify the number of data bytes to be sent. The default is 56, which translates into 64 ICMP data bytes when combined with the 8 bytes of ICMP header data.

options.name: -T
options.description: Set the IP Time To Live for multicasted packets. This flag only applies if the ping destination is a multicast address

options.name: -t
options.description: Specify a timeout, in seconds, before ping exits regardless of how many packets have been received

options.name: -v
options.description: Verbose output. ICMP packets other than ECHO_RESPONSE that are received are listed

options.name: -W
options.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for a reply for each packet sent.

options.name: -z
options.description: Use the specified type of service

options.name: --apple-connect
options.description: Connects the socket to the destination address

options.name: --apple-time
options.description: Prints the time a packet was received
